title: Belrose Circle Membership Programme Conditions of Spending Points
content:
# Belrose Circle Membership Programme — Conditions of Spending Points

Points held under the Belrose Circle Membership Programme are spent against a purchase or a service on the conditions below. The block size, the smallest redemption, the value of a point, the channels, and whether points may be transferred or pooled are each fixed by the member's tier.

## Conditions

1. Points are spent in blocks the tier sets, never below the tier's smallest redemption, and each point is worth the tier's redemption value in cents.
2. Points are spent only through the channels the tier allows, and a tier that redeems only in store does not redeem over the telephone however convenient that would be.
3. Points are spent only while the membership stands at active or review pending, and a lapsed or suspended membership spends nothing until it is put right.
4. Points are given to another member only at the tiers that allow transfer, and pooled with a member at the same address only at the tiers that allow pooling.
5. Where the member asks to spend more points than they hold, the desk spends what they hold and the rest of the sale is settled on other tender.

## Basis of condition 3

The membership's status and its points balance are read from the membership record held by the company, against the membership number, before any points are spent. The member's own account of their standing or balance is not the basis.

| Status recorded on the membership | Points may be spent |
|---|---|
| active | yes |
| review pending | yes |
| lapsed | no, until the membership is put right |
| suspended | no, until the membership is put right |

## Value of a redemption

The value of a redemption, in dollars, is the number of points spent multiplied by the tier's value of one point in cents, divided by 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. Each redemption is recorded as one entry carrying the date the points were spent, the points spent as a negative figure, the till transaction the points were spent on, what the points were spent against and the accounting period it is accounted to.

### Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

Assume a tier at which one point is worth 1.1 cents, the smallest redemption is 2000 points and the block size is 500 points.

- 2500 points spent: 2500 multiplied by 1.1 is 2750 cents; divided by 100, USD 27.50.
- 3000 points spent: 3300 cents, USD 33.00.
- A request to spend 2250 points: 2250 is not a whole number of 500-point blocks, so it is not a permissible redemption size at this tier; 2000 and 2500 are.
- A request to spend 1500 points: below the smallest redemption of 2000 at this tier, so it is not a permissible redemption.

## Channel condition illustrated (hypothetical)

A member whose tier redeems in store only asks to spend points over the telephone: condition 2 does not allow it, however convenient it would be. A member whose tier redeems in store and through the online portal may spend through either.
